T1.mapping_reason: CA-ALG-01 is the AB 325 common pricing algorithm ban (Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729), effective 2026-01-01. That date falls between the test's before and after dates. SB 763 is named in the title but we have no separate record for it, so only CA-ALG-01 is mapped.
T1.notes: Results for CA-ALG-01 compared on 2025-12-31 and 2026-01-02. 250 addresses change.

T2.mapping_reason: HOB-ALG-01 is Hoboken's algorithmic rent coordination ban (City Code ch. 158-2). JC-ALG-01 is Jersey City's algorithmic rent-setting ban (Code § 218-12). Both are in force before 2026-10-01. Listed in the test's order.
T2.notes: Addresses covered by HOB-ALG-01, JC-ALG-01 on 2026-10-01. 90 addresses.

T3.mapping_reason: NJ-ALG-01 is the NJ FAIR Act (P.L. 2026, c. 43). It is marked not yet effective, with an effective date of 2027-07-01, which falls between the test's before and after dates. The rules to check for conflicts are the Jersey City and Hoboken local bans, in the test's order.
T3.notes: Results for NJ-ALG-01 compared on 2026-10-01 and 2027-07-02. 140 addresses change.

T4.mapping_reason: Both are pending Massachusetts bills. The order is a guess: the test's ids don't name the bills, so I assumed MA-ALG-P1 is S.2983 and MA-ALG-P2 is H.5222, following the title's order. That gives MA-ALG-02 (S.2983) then MA-ALG-01 (H.5222). Please confirm against the source.
T4.notes: MA-ALG-02, MA-ALG-01 reported as pending, never in force; affected = addresses covered if enacted. 110 addresses.

T5.mapping_reason: MA-RENT-02 is Initiative Petition 25-21, the statewide cap on rent increases. It is marked failed because it was blocked from the November 2026 ballot (Cella v. Attorney General, SJC-13893). This matches the struck rent-control ballot question.
T5.notes: MA-RENT-02 is not law on 2026-10-01; no address gets it. 0 addresses.
